summary: The milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 experiment commits since activation (total_wall_time_minutes=0, experiments_completed=0, compute_bound_experiments_count=0), but on-disk verification shows real 2026.06.447 research-arm artifacts WERE written this window. This is the recurring FALSE-ZERO detector observability gap (the shipped detector-wire reaches the standalone module but not the conductor's retro prompt-assembly call site that feeds the retro TIMING DATA block), NOT a genuinely empty or capstone-only milestone. Both RTX 3090s idle (0% util) is correct: no monitored-3090 compute-bound task ran (the one live arm used the AMD iGPU sprint generator; the rest were aggregation / cached-candidate verifier-scoring / hardware-smoke), so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null and GPU idle is not flagged.
bottlenecks_identified: OBSERVABILITY, not execution: the milestone-scoped commit detector false-reported zero experiment commits since activation while real .447 arm artifacts exist on disk for this window. This recurring false-zero gap (seen across many prior milestones) is the only operational defect; experiment execution itself proceeded normally to a clean capstone.

GPU idle is NOT flagged as a bottleneck: 0% util with no monitored-3090 compute-bound task present is expected per the GPU-idle interpretation rule. The live arm ran on the iGPU sprint stack, and the remaining arms had no GPU code path (aggregation / cached-candidate verifier-scoring / hardware-smoke).
improvements_suggested: MOVE the shipped milestone-scoped detector-wire to the conductor's retro TIMING-DATA prompt-assembly call site so the retro receives real per-arm timing instead of a false zero.

Add a disk-mtime fallback: when the commit-scan window returns zero, scan results/experiment_*.json mtimes within [activation, now] so a detector false-zero degrades to a verifiable artifact-mtime window rather than a misleading empty block.
Stamp duration_s / inference_substrate / compute_bound at artifact write-time on every arm so the retro can classify GPU-idle correctness mechanically without re-reading each file.
Pass a milestone_type hint (research vs capstone/docs) into the retro input so a genuinely-empty just-activated window is never confused with a false-zero detector gap.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Wire the milestone-scoped timing detector into the conductor's retro prompt-assembly call site and add a disk-mtime fallback — the recurring highest-leverage fix that ends the false-zero gap for good.
Stamp duration_s / inference_substrate / compute_bound at artifact write-time so GPU-idle correctness and the compute-bound count are mechanically derivable instead of re-inferred each milestone.

Keep the idle dual-3090 capacity ready via DualGPURunner for any next milestone that loads 2+ models; current live arms correctly used the iGPU sprint stack, so the 3090 idle is not a regression to chase.
meta_reflection: The retro's own input is the defect this milestone, not the experiments: real .447 arms executed and the capstone shipped clean, yet the timing detector reported a false zero — the same observability gap recurring for dozens of milestones. The locked 0/0/0/null fields are the detector's output, not ground truth; the durable fix is to wire the detector into the conductor's retro prompt-assembly path and add a disk-mtime fallback so an empty TIMING DATA block can never again be misread as an empty milestone.
